passage:
Mandy hated history dates, but she loved stories. Her teacher suggested a history podcast about ordinary people in the past.
The first episode was about a street cleaner during a war. The second was about a woman who repaired radios. The third was about children who wrote letters during a long journey.
Mandy realized history was not only about rulers and battles. It was also about people trying to live through difficult times.
Later, when her textbook mentioned the same period, the dates felt less empty. They connected to faces and choices.
A podcast did not replace study, but it gave history a heartbeat. Facts became easier to remember when they belonged to people.
